ec-249.title: Izmir Meatballs in Tomato Sauce (İzmir Köftesi)
ec-249.culturalNotes: Recipe 249, page 113 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-249-i10.name: Sauce: Sweet Green Pepper, Very Finely Diced

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with cold water and squeeze it out.
instructions.2: Mince the bread twice with the beef, onions, parsley, garlic, cumin, salt and pepper, then knead in the egg.
instructions.3: With wet hands, shape round or oval balls and roll them very lightly in seasoned flour.
instructions.4: Fry the meatballs lightly and drain them on absorbent paper.
instructions.5: Soften the green pepper in the same oil, add the tomato juice, sugar, salt and pepper and cook for 10–12 minutes.
instructions.6: Return the meatballs and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce thickens.

ec-261.title: Upper Egyptian Mashed Okra with Beef and Chili (Bamya Weeka Sa‘idi)
ec-261.culturalNotes: Recipe 261, page 118 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into small cubes and boil it in the stock for 20–30 minutes, until tender. Lift it out.
instructions.2: Add the okra and chilies to the broth, cook for about 10 minutes, then mash with a fork.
instructions.3: Return the meat to the pot.
instructions.4: Make the ta’liya: pound the garlic with the coriander, salt and pepper and fry it in the oil for 3–5 minutes. Tip it into the pot, swirl a spoonful of broth round the frying pan and add that too.
instructions.5: Simmer for 5–7 minutes and serve.

ec-265.title: Iraqi Okra Stew with Tamarind (Bamia Marag)
ec-265.culturalNotes: Recipe 265, page 119 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-265-i7.name: Cumin, Coriander, Cinnamon, Cloves And Peppercorns

instructions.1: Cut the mutton into bite-sized cubes and boil with the spices until tender. Lift it out, keeping the broth.
instructions.2: Fry the mutton in ghee, then add the okra and garlic and stir until everything is well fried.
instructions.3: Dissolve the tomato paste in the tamarind liquid, season, and add it to the pot with the broth.
instructions.4: Simmer for 30 minutes.
instructions.5: Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice.

ec-266.title: Oven-Roasted Pearl Onions (’Awirma Mashwiya)
ec-266.culturalNotes: Recipe 266, page 120 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Put the onions, still in their skins, in a hot oven for about an hour, until thoroughly cooked.
instructions.2: Peel them at the table; they should be soft enough to melt in the mouth.

ec-267.title: Pearl Onion and Beef Casserole (Tagin ’Awirma)
ec-267.culturalNotes: Recipe 267, page 120 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into small cubes. Peel the garlic and halve it diagonally.
instructions.2: Fry the beef and onions lightly in oil and move them to a casserole.
instructions.3: Add the garlic, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cover with the stock.
instructions.4: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 90–120 minutes.
instructions.5: Thicken the gravy with cornflour if you like.
instructions.6: Sweet-sour version (recipe 268 in the book): use 2 cups of tomato juice instead of stock, with 1 teaspoon each of sugar and vinegar dissolved in it, and spice with cinnamon or nutmeg.

ec-271.title: Meat-Filled Gullash Fingers (Asabi‘ Gullash bi-l-Lahma)
ec-271.culturalNotes: Recipe 271, page 122 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Make the savory minced beef: fry the onion in a little oil until pale gold, add the beef, salt and pepper and cook until the juices are absorbed. You need about 1 cup.
instructions.2: Cut the gullash into 10 cm squares and keep them under a cloth so they do not dry out.
instructions.3: Working one square at a time, lay a narrow strip of meat across the middle, stopping 1 cm from each end.
instructions.4: Fold in the ends and roll up very tightly.
instructions.5: Pack the fingers into a greased baking pan and brush the tops with melted butter.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven until golden.

ec-273.title: Crisp Layered Ruqaq with Cheese and Egg (Saniyit Ru’a’ bi-l-Gibna)
ec-273.culturalNotes: Recipe 273, page 123 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Grate the Balkan cheese. Mash the areesh cheese with the hard-boiled eggs, then mix in the grated cheese, the beaten raw egg and a pinch of pepper.
instructions.2: Grease a deep baking pan (you will need a second pan the same size). Dip one ruqaq sheet at a time in hot broth and use them to line the pan, sprinkling each layer with a little oil.
instructions.3: After 3–4 layers, spread the cheese filling evenly, then carry on with more dipped, oiled layers.
instructions.4: Pour any remaining oil over the top and bake in a moderate oven.
instructions.5: When the top is brown, turn it over into the second pan and return it to the oven to brown the other side.

ec-275.title: Lamb and Lisan ‘Asfur Pasta Casserole (Tagin Lisan ‘Asfur)
ec-275.culturalNotes: Recipe 275, page 124 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the meat into bite-sized cubes. Seed the peppers and slice them thinly.
instructions.2: Sauté the onion in the butter and oil, add the lamb and fry until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Cover with stock, add the peppers, cinnamon, salt and pepper and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.4: Lift out the meat and vegetables with a slotted spoon and put them in an ovenproof pot.
instructions.5: Parboil the lisan ‘asfur in the stock for 5–7 minutes and pour it over the meat, adding hot water if it is not covered.
instructions.6: Bake in a moderate, preheated oven for 30 minutes.

ec-281.title: Shishbarak (Meat Dumplings in Garlic Yogurt)
ec-281.culturalNotes: Recipe 281, page 127 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sift the flour with salt and add enough water to knead a smooth dough that comes away from the bowl. Rest it for an hour.
instructions.2: Fry the pine nuts golden and set aside. Soften the onion in the same oil, add the meat and fry until its juices are gone, then stir in the pine nuts, spices, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Roll the dough out on a floured surface and cut it into small rounds.
instructions.4: Put 1/2 teaspoon of filling on each, fold into a crescent with wet fingers, then wrap it round your finger and pinch the ends together so it looks like a little hat.
instructions.5: Set them on a greased tray, brush with ghee and bake in a moderate oven until crisp and golden.
instructions.6: Fry the garlic in a little ghee until golden, stirring constantly, and stir in the mint.
instructions.7: Whisk the egg whites until frothy and mix them into the yogurt to keep it from splitting. Heat it uncovered over a low heat and add the garlic mixture.
instructions.8: When the yogurt bubbles, add the shishbarak and cook for 7–10 minutes more.

ec-283.title: Layered Peas, Rice and Minced Beef Béchamel (Basilla bi-l-Bechamel)
ec-283.culturalNotes: Recipe 283, page 128 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Parboil the peas in salted water for 10 minutes and drain.
instructions.2: Grease a deep ovenproof serving dish, preferably glass.
instructions.3: Arrange the rice, peas and minced beef in several thin layers, moistening every layer with béchamel.
instructions.4: Pour the beaten egg over the top.
instructions.5: Bake in the middle of a moderate, preheated oven for 20–30 minutes, until browned on top.

ec-308.title: Brown Onion Rice for Fish (Ruzz Ahmar)
ec-308.culturalNotes: Recipe 308, page 137 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the rice in warm water for 15–20 minutes and drain.
instructions.2: Fry the onions in the oil until deep brown.
instructions.3: Add the water and salt and bring to the boil.
instructions.4: Stir in the rice, cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.5: For a redder rice (recipe 309 in the book), stir 1 tablespoon of tomato paste into the water before adding the rice.

ec-310.title: Rice Cooked in Shrimp Stock (Ruzz bi-Salsit Gambari)
ec-310.culturalNotes: Recipe 310, page 138 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rinse the shrimp under running water until it runs clear. Put them in a pot with the onions, lemons, cumin, salt and pepper, without any water, and cook over a moderate heat, tossing every few minutes, for about 7 minutes or until done.
instructions.2: Cool and shell the shrimp, keeping the heads, shells and juices. Remove the dark vein.
instructions.3: Make the shrimp sauce: blend the heads, shells and juices at high speed and strain. You need 1 cup.
instructions.4: Fry the rice in the oil, stirring until every grain is coated.
instructions.5: Add 2 cups of water and the cup of shrimp sauce. It is already well seasoned, so add no salt.
instructions.6: Cook uncovered over a moderate heat until the liquid is absorbed, then cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 20–30 minutes.

ec-311.title: Rice with Tomatoes, Peppers and Carrots (Ruzz bi-l-Khudar)
ec-311.culturalNotes: Recipe 311, page 138 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-311-i4.name: Sweet Green Peppers, Blanched And Thinly Sliced

instructions.1: Sauté the onion until golden and mix it with the tomatoes, peppers and carrots.
instructions.2: Fry the rice in the same oil, stirring, until every grain is coated.
instructions.3: Add the vegetables, water, salt and pepper and stir one last time.
instructions.4: Cook uncovered over a high heat until the water is absorbed.
instructions.5: Cover, turn the heat to its lowest and cook for 15–20 minutes.

ec-313.title: Soft Rice Porridge with Beef (Ruzz Lubba bi-l-Lahma)
ec-313.culturalNotes: Recipe 313, page 139 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the beef into bite-sized cubes.
instructions.2: Fry the onions until golden, add the beef and fry over a high heat until its juices are absorbed.
instructions.3: Season, add water to cover and cook over a low heat for 15–20 minutes.
instructions.4: Top up the water to 4–5 cups, stir in the rice and check the seasoning.
instructions.5: Cover and cook slowly for about 30 minutes. It should end up soft and porridge-like.
instructions.6: With gizzards (recipe 314 in the book): stir 5–6 mastic grains into hot oil for 10–15 seconds, add halved boiled gizzards, cover and turn off the heat for 1–2 minutes, then fry them, add 4 cups of water and the rice and cook the same way.

ec-315.title: Turkish Eggplant Pilaf (Patlıcanlı Pilav)
ec-315.culturalNotes: Recipe 315, page 140 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Dice the eggplant without peeling, salt it and leave for an hour. Squeeze out the moisture and pat dry.
instructions.2: Fry the eggplant until lightly browned and drain on absorbent paper.
instructions.3: Soften the chopped onion in the same oil, then add the tomatoes, parsley, mint, eggplant, salt and pepper and bring to the boil.
instructions.4: Add the rice and enough water to cover.
instructions.5: Boil hard, then lower the heat and simmer gently for 30 minutes.

ec-317.title: Saffron Rice Kibbeh (Kubbat Halab)
ec-317.culturalNotes: Recipe 317, page 141 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-317-i5.name: Celery Or Parsley, Very Finely Chopped

instructions.1: Boil the rice in 4 cups of water with the saffron and salt until soft, breaking up any lumps with a fork. Drain off any water left.
instructions.2: Add the lightly beaten egg and, with fingers dipped in the turmeric rose water, knead the rice into a soft dough that holds its shape.
instructions.3: Filling: fry the beef, then add the celery or parsley, almonds, raisins, mixed spice, salt and pepper and cook together over a low heat for 10 minutes.
instructions.4: Take a little rice dough in your palm, moistened with rose water, and hollow it out with a finger of the other hand, turning it into a thin cup.
instructions.5: Fill with the meat, close it into an oval ball with a moistened palm and set it on a floured surface. Repeat until the dough is used up.

ec-318.title: Persian Crusty Steamed Rice with Yogurt Tahdig (Chelow Dig)
ec-318.culturalNotes: Recipe 318, page 141 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the rice in boiling water and drain.
instructions.2: Bring 8 cups of heavily salted water to the boil, add the rice, cook for 5 minutes, then drain and rinse in hot water.
instructions.3: Stir the yogurt into one cup of the half-cooked rice.
instructions.4: Swirl a tablespoon of ghee round the base and sides of a heavy pan and spread the yogurt rice over the bottom.
instructions.5: Pile the rest of the rice on top, sprinkle with the remaining ghee and steam over a moderate heat, breaking up any clusters, until tender and crusty underneath.
instructions.6: Mound the steamed rice in the middle of a dish and break the golden crust from the bottom of the pan into pieces around it.

ec-320.title: Everyday Egyptian Salad Dressing (Khalta li-l-Salata)
ec-320.culturalNotes: Recipe 320, page 142 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Mix all the ingredients together.
instructions.2: Pour over the salad just before serving.

ec-323.title: Fresh Cabbage Salad with Garlic and Lemon (Salatit Krumb)
ec-323.culturalNotes: Recipe 323, page 143 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the cabbage and onion with salt and rub well, then rinse and drain.
instructions.2: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and salt.
instructions.3: Pour over the vegetables and toss.

ec-329.title: Egyptian Chopped Salad (Salata Baladi)
ec-329.culturalNotes: Recipe 329, page 145 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-329-i11.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Only onions and tomatoes are essential; add whatever else the season offers.
instructions.2: Chop everything finely, keeping each vegetable separate.
instructions.3: Rub the onion with salt, rinse it and leave it to soak in lemon juice.
instructions.4: Rub the inside of the salad bowl with the cut garlic clove and heap the vegetables in it.
instructions.5: Just before serving, add the dressing and toss.

ec-331.title: Artichoke and Egg Salad (Salatit Kharshuf)
ec-331.culturalNotes: Recipe 331, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-331-i3.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Boil the artichoke hearts in salted water until tender, drain and chop.
instructions.2: Add them to the chopped eggs.
instructions.3: Pour over the dressing and mix well.

ec-332.title: Green Bean Salad with Red Onion (Salatit Fasulya Khadra)
ec-332.culturalNotes: Recipe 332, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: String the beans and trim the tops and tails.
instructions.2: Boil in salted water until tender, drain and spread out to cool.
instructions.3: Put the sliced onion in the salad bowl to soak in the lemon juice.
instructions.4: Before serving, add the beans and oil and mix.

ec-333.title: Beetroot Salad with Garlic Vinegar (Salatit Bangar bi-l-Toom)
ec-333.culturalNotes: Recipe 333, page 146 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Boil the beetroot for about an hour, until very tender.
instructions.2: Drain, keeping two tablespoons of the cooking water. Cool, peel and cut into small cubes, thin slices or fingers.
instructions.3: Crush the garlic with salt until very smooth and mix in the vinegar.
instructions.4: Stir the garlic dressing into the reserved cooking water, pour over the beetroot and mix gently.
instructions.5: With tahini (recipe 334 in the book): dress the beetroot with 2 tablespoons of thin tahini sauce instead.
instructions.6: With yogurt (recipe 335 in the book): mix the cubed beetroot with 3 diced tomatoes and 3–5 diced cucumbers and cover with 1 cup of garlic yogurt (yogurt, crushed garlic and salt, without mint).

ec-336.title: Blanched Cabbage Salad with Salted Fish (Salatit Krumb)
ec-336.culturalNotes: Recipe 336, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-336-i3.name: Salad Dressing (oil, Lemon, Vinegar, Salt And Pepper)

instructions.1: Shred the cabbage very finely, blanch it for 1 minute, drain and cool.
instructions.2: Chop the fish very finely and stir it into the dressing.
instructions.3: Pour over the cabbage and mix well.

ec-337.title: Wilted Spinach Salad with Onion and Lemon (Salatit Sabanikh)
ec-337.culturalNotes: Recipe 337, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Chop the spinach leaves and stems coarsely, sprinkle with salt and rub until they lose some juice. Rinse and pat dry.
instructions.2: Wilt the spinach over a low heat, drain and spread out to cool.
instructions.3: Mix in the onion, lemon juice, oil and salt.

ec-338.title: Turkish Spinach Salad with Feta (Ispanak Salatası)
ec-338.culturalNotes: Recipe 338, page 147 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Rinse the spinach, chop it coarsely and wilt it in a pot over the heat.
instructions.2: Drain in a colander, pressing with a spoon to squeeze out the moisture, and put it in a bowl.
instructions.3: Fry the onions in the olive oil until golden and add them to the bowl.
instructions.4: Add the parsley, cheese, salt and pepper and toss well.

ec-342.title: Brown Onion Sauce (Salsa Bunniya)
ec-342.culturalNotes: Recipe 342, page 149 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Melt the butter with the oil over a low heat and fry the onion until deep brown. Lift the onion out and set aside.
instructions.2: Stir the flour into the fat until well blended and cook it.
instructions.3: Add the stock a little at a time, stirring constantly, until you have a smooth, thin cream.
instructions.4: Return the onion, season, and cook on, adding more stock for a thin, smooth sauce.

ec-344.title: Dried Kishk Cakes for Storing (Kishk li-l-Takhzin)
ec-344.culturalNotes: Recipe 344, page 150 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Dissolve the salt in the milk.
instructions.2: Gradually work in the sifted flour until you have a thick dough that comes cleanly away from the bowl.
instructions.3: Leave it to ferment for 4–5 days, sprinkling flour over the top.
instructions.4: Shape it into small, flat round cakes and dry them in the open air for a few days, turning each cake twice a day, until very hard.
instructions.5: Store in a tightly closed box, as cakes or pounded to a powder, ready to cook into kishk.
instructions.6: With yogurt (recipe 345 in the book): make it the same way with yogurt instead of milk. As yogurt is already fermented it needs only 2–3 days, and the taste is quite different.
instructions.7: Upper Egyptian kishk (recipe 346 in the book): rinse fine bulgur and spread it to dry, then cover it with salted soured milk in a large earthenware pot for 5 days, adding more soured milk every 24 hours. On the sixth day knead it into a stiff dough, shape small round cakes and dry them the same way.

ec-353.title: Cypriot Garlic and Almond Sauce (Skordalia)
ec-353.culturalNotes: Recipe 353, page 152 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl.
instructions.2: Soak the garlic in the vinegar for 10 minutes, then add it to the bread with the almonds, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Beat in the lemon juice and oil alternately, in thin streams, until the sauce is as thick as custard.

ec-354.title: Turkish Hazelnut Tarator Sauce
ec-354.culturalNotes: Recipe 354, page 153 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Sprinkle the bread with water, squeeze it out and crumble it into a bowl. Add the hazelnuts and garlic.
instructions.2: Beat in the vinegar, salt and oil alternately, in a thin stream, until the sauce is like a thin custard.
instructions.3: Chill before using.
instructions.4: Hazelnuts are the original, but a mix of pine nuts, almonds and/or walnuts is also used, in which case use lemon juice instead of vinegar.

ec-355.title: Gulf Spiced Onion Sauce for Grilled Meat (Sharmoola)
ec-355.culturalNotes: Recipe 355, page 153 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Heat the oil and cook the ginger, saffron, cumin and hot pepper in it for 1–2 minutes.
instructions.2: Lower the heat and add the onions, salt, garlic, parsley and coriander.
instructions.3: Cook, stirring constantly, until everything is soft and well blended.

ec-356.title: Cypriot Tomato Sauce with Cinnamon and Bay (Saltsa Tomata)
ec-356.culturalNotes: Recipe 356, page 154 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Fry the onion until golden, add the tomatoes and cook for 3–5 minutes.
instructions.2: Thin the tomato paste with an equal amount of water and add it with the sugar, bay leaf, cinnamon, salt and pepper.
instructions.3: Cook uncovered for 20 minutes, until thick.
instructions.4: Remove the bay leaf and cinnamon before using.

ec-361.title: Crabs Steamed with Lemon and Onion (Kaburya)
ec-361.culturalNotes: Recipe 361, page 156 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the crabs under running water.
instructions.2: Put everything in a pot, without any water, over a low heat.
instructions.3: Toss from time to time; depending on their size the crabs should be done in 7–10 minutes.
instructions.4: Eat them just as they are: crack the shells of the body and legs and pick out the meat.

ec-364.title: Cumin Batter-Fried Baby Shrimp (Gambari Ma’li)
ec-364.culturalNotes: Recipe 364, page 157 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Wash the shrimp well and peel them.
instructions.2: Mix the flour, milk, water, egg and cumin into a thin batter.
instructions.3: Dip the shrimp in the batter and deep-fry in very hot oil.
instructions.4: Drain on absorbent paper and sprinkle with salt and cumin.

ec-366.title: Egyptian Chicken Soup with Mastic and Cardamom (Shurbit Firakh)
ec-366.culturalNotes: Recipe 366, page 158 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Tie the cardamom and mastic in a muslin bag.
instructions.2: Bring 3 cups of water to the boil with the onions and spice bag.
instructions.3: Lower in the chicken, season and turn down the heat.
instructions.4: When the chicken is tender, lift it out, discard the spice bag and mash the onion into the broth.
instructions.5: Add the rice or vermicelli and cook for 12–15 minutes.
instructions.6: Palestinian version (recipe 367 in the book): just before serving, add 1–2 tablespoons of pine nuts and 1/2 cup of parsley leaves and heat without boiling.

ec-373.title: Turkish Wedding Soup (Düğün Çorbası)
ec-373.culturalNotes: Recipe 373, page 160 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes, roll them in seasoned flour and fry.
instructions.2: Add the lamb to the broth, bring to the boil and add the carrot, onion and seasoning. Simmer for about an hour.
instructions.3: Lift out the meat, keep back one ladleful of soup to cool, and mash the vegetables into the rest. Return the meat and keep the soup over a very low heat.
instructions.4: Beat the egg yolks with the lemon juice, then beat in the cooled ladleful of soup.
instructions.5: Stir the egg mixture into the soup and heat for 2–3 minutes. Do not let it boil or the eggs will curdle.

ec-374.title: Tunisian Fish and Barley Soup (Chorba bil Hout)
ec-374.culturalNotes: Recipe 374, page 160 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

ec-374-i2.name: Fish Head, Backbone, Tail And Trimmings

ec-374-i8.name: Celery Leaves And Stalks, Coarsely Chopped

instructions.1: Cover the fish head, bones and trimmings with water and bring to the boil, skimming as needed.
instructions.2: Boil the barley in salted water for 30 minutes, drain and keep warm.
instructions.3: Fry the fillets lightly and set them aside. Soften the onions in the same oil, add the tomato paste and stir for 2–3 minutes.
instructions.4: Add this to the fish stock with the garlic, cumin, coriander, paprika, parsley, celery, salt and pepper and boil for 20 minutes.
instructions.5: Let it cool, remove the fish pieces, blend the liquid and strain it through a very fine sieve, ideally lined with muslin.
instructions.6: Return to the pot with the barley and fish fillets, check the seasoning and boil for 7–10 minutes, until the fish is cooked.
instructions.7: Add the lemon juice and serve.

ec-376.title: Gulf Mutton, Chickpea and Vermicelli Soup (Tchorba)
ec-376.culturalNotes: Recipe 376, page 162 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas in water overnight.
instructions.2: Fry the cutlets in ghee, then add everything except the vermicelli, cover with twice their volume of water and cook until tender.
instructions.3: Take out the cutlets, mash the vegetables and return the cutlets to the pot.
instructions.4: When the soup boils, check the seasoning, add the vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes more, until it is tender and has taken on the flavour of the soup.

ec-377.title: Tunisian Hlalem Noodle Soup with Lamb and Vegetables
ec-377.culturalNotes: Recipe 377, page 162 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas and fava beans for a few hours. Drain, then boil with the onion in twice their volume of water for 15 minutes. Set aside with their liquid.
instructions.2: Cut the lamb into bite-sized cubes and fry in olive oil. Add the scallions and garlic and cook for 5 minutes, stirring constantly.
instructions.3: Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 5 minutes, then add the spinach, celery, parsley, artichokes, carrots, paprika, salt and pepper and stir until coated.
instructions.4: Add the chickpeas and beans with their liquid and simmer for 30–45 minutes. Cool and skim off any excess fat.
instructions.5: About an hour before serving, bring back to the boil, adding more salted water if needed, then add the hlalem and sweet peppers. Cover and simmer until the noodles are plump and soft.
instructions.6: Add the peas, check the seasoning and sprinkle with fresh coriander.

ec-380.title: Egyptian Chickpea Soup with Cumin and Lemon (Shurbit Hummus)
ec-380.culturalNotes: Recipe 380, page 164 from Egyptian Cooking and Other Middle Eastern Recipes (Samia Abdennour, AUC Press)

instructions.1: Soak the chickpeas overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Cover with twice their volume of fresh water, add the onions and cook for 20–30 minutes, until tender.
instructions.3: Add the cumin, lemon juice, salt and pepper and boil for 3–5 minutes more.
instructions.4: Serve with croutons of baladi bread.
